Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 77, verses 16–28:

﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ He means among the disobedient. There are two views about who is meant:

The first: the people of Noah, peace be upon him, because their destruction by the flood was the most widely known and the most general.

The second: that it refers to the people of every prophet who were uprooted, because that is rarer among nations.

﴿Then We follow them with the later ones.﴾ He means that they were destroyed for their disobedience like the former ones, either by the sword or by annihilation.

﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals.﴾ This may carry two meanings:

The first: that it is a grave warning of their destruction in this world, as a lesson.

The second: that it is an announcement of their punishment in the Hereafter, as what they deserve.

﴿Did We not create you from a despised water?﴾ On this there are three views:

The first: from the purest part of the water, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: from weak water, as said by Mujahid and Qatadah.

The third: from flowing semen, as said by Ibn Kamil.

﴿Then We placed it in a firm abode.﴾ On this there are two views:

The first: as said by Wahb ibn Munabbih, in the womb of its mother, where neither heat nor cold harms it.

The second: "firm" means secure and well-guarded, not returning and coming out, nor spreading through the body so that it would persist. This was said by al-Kalbi.

﴿For a known term.﴾ Until the day of its birth.

﴿Then We determined, and how excellent are the determiners!﴾ In the recitation of Nafi', it is read with the shadda (doubled letter, faqadarna). The rest read it without the shadda (qadarna). Whoever reads it without the shadda, its interpretation is: "then We possessed, and how excellent are the possessors." Whoever reads it with the shadda, its interpretation is: "then We decreed, and how excellent are the decreers." Al-Farra' said: "They are two dialects, and their meaning is one."

﴿Did We not make the earth a receptacle?﴾ On this there are four interpretations:

The first: it means a shelter, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: a covering, as said by Mujahid.

The third: a gathering place, as said by al-Mufaddal.

The fourth: a vessel. Al-Samsamah ibn al-Tirimmah said:

"Today you are alive upon the earth, but tomorrow it will gather you into its receptacle."

﴿Both the living and the dead.﴾ On this there are two views:

The first: that the earth gathers people alive on its surface and dead within its belly, as said by Qatadah and al-Sha'bi.

The second: that from the earth come the living, through cultivation and plants, and the dead, through barrenness and drought. This is one of the two opinions of Mujahid.

﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ He means among the disobedient. There are two views about who is meant:

The first: the people of Noah, peace be upon him, because their destruction by the flood was the most widely known and the most general.

The second: that it refers to the people of every prophet who were uprooted, because that is rarer among nations.

﴿Then We follow them with the later ones.﴾ He means that they were destroyed for their disobedience like the former ones, either by the sword or by annihilation.

﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals.﴾ This may carry two meanings:

The first: that it is a grave warning of their destruction in this world, as a lesson.

The second: that it is an announcement of their punishment in the Hereafter, as what they deserve.

﴿Did We not create you from a despised water?﴾ On this there are three views:

The first: from the purest part of the water, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: from weak water, as said by Mujahid and Qatadah.

The third: from flowing semen, as said by Ibn Kamil.

﴿Then We placed it in a firm abode.﴾ On this there are two views:

The first: as said by Wahb ibn Munabbih, in the womb of its mother, where neither heat nor cold harms it.

The second: "firm" means secure and well-guarded, not returning and coming out, nor spreading through the body so that it would persist. This was said by al-Kalbi.

﴿For a known term.﴾ Until the day of its birth.

﴿Then We determined, and how excellent are the determiners!﴾ In the recitation of Nafi', it is read with the shadda (doubled letter, faqadarna). The rest read it without the shadda (qadarna). Whoever reads it without the shadda, its interpretation is: "then We possessed, and how excellent are the possessors." Whoever reads it with the shadda, its interpretation is: "then We decreed, and how excellent are the decreers." Al-Farra' said: "They are two dialects, and their meaning is one."

﴿Did We not make the earth a receptacle?﴾ On this there are four interpretations:

The first: it means a shelter, as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: a covering, as said by Mujahid.

The third: a gathering place, as said by al-Mufaddal.

The fourth: a vessel. Al-Samsamah ibn al-Tirimmah said:

"Today you are alive upon the earth, but tomorrow it will gather you into its receptacle."

﴿Both the living and the dead.﴾ On this there are two views:

The first: that the earth gathers people alive on its surface and dead within its belly, as said by Qatadah and al-Sha'bi.

The second: that from the earth come the living, through cultivation and plants, and the dead, through barrenness and drought. This is one of the two opinions of Mujahid.

﴿Proceed to a shadow of three branches﴾. It is said that a branch will be above it, a branch on its right, and a branch on its left, enclosing it. This is the view of Mujahid.

The second view: the three branches are the *darii* (a thorny plant), the *zaqqum* (a bitter tree), and the *ghislin* (the pus of the damned). This is the view of al-Dahhak.

It is also possible that a third view is intended: the three branches are the flame (*lahab*), the sparks (*sharar*), and the smoke (*dukhan*), because these are three states that represent the most extreme descriptions of the Fire when it blazes and intensifies.

﴿Neither cool nor sheltering﴾, meaning it provides no protection from harm.

﴿And it does not shield from the flame﴾. The *lahab* is what rises above the Fire when it blazes, in red, yellow, and green.

﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a castle﴾. The *sharar* is what flies off as fragments of fire. Regarding His words ﴿like a castle﴾, there are five interpretations.

The first: they are the great roots of trees. This is the view of al-Dahhak.

The second: like a mountain. This is the view of Muqatil.

The third: *al-qasr* is a building, the singular of *qusur* (palaces). This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

The fourth: it is a piece of wood that the people of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic era) used to aim at, about three cubits long, which they called *al-qasr*. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The fifth: they are the necks of camels. This is the view of Qatadah.

It is also possible to take a sixth interpretation: that this is a descriptive term of magnification, referring to it by the name *al-qasr* because of the awe it inspires in souls, even though no specific referent is intended.

﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations. The first: it means yellow camels, and by "yellow" is meant black; they were called yellow because their blackness tends toward yellowness. This is the view of al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatadah. A poet said:

"Those are my horses from it, and those are my mounts; their young are yellow like raisins."

The second: they are the ropes of ships. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The third: they are pieces of copper. This is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

As for naming them "yellow camels," there are two explanations:

One: because of the swiftness of their movement.

Two: because some of them follow others in succession.

﴿So if you have a plot, then plot against Me﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations.

The first: if you have a stratagem, then devise one for yourselves. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second: if you are able to keep yourselves away from Me, then do so. This is the meaning of the statement of al-Kalbi.
